landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (Methow Valley Ranger District)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at Washington Pass Overlook, Blue Lake, and Cutthroat trailheads — $5/day or $30/annual (America the Beautiful pass also honored).
drive: From Seattle, drive I-5 north to Burlington/Sedro-Woolley, then east on SR-20 through Marblemount and over Rainy Pass to Washington Pass; from Winthrop/Mazama it's a quick 20-30 minute drive west on SR-20 instead.

names: Hannegan Pass Trailhead (end of Ruth Creek Rd / FR-32), via Hannegan Pass, Chilliwack River Trail, Whatcom Pass and Perfect Pass to the SW side of Phantom Peak
landManager: National Park Service — North Cascades National Park (Stephen Mather Wilderness)
storedPass: None inside the park; a Northwest Forest Pass may be required at some adjacent national forest trailheads.
drive: From the Mount Baker Highway (SR-542), turn onto Hannegan Pass Road (FR-32) and drive 5.3 miles to the trailhead at the end of the road

landManager: National Park Service
storedPass: Not a Northwest Forest Pass (that's a USFS pass and doesn't apply inside the park). Standard NPS entrance fee applies: $30/vehicle (7 consecutive days), $55 Mount Rainier annual pass, or $80 America the Beautiful interagency annual pass.
drive: From Elbe, drive SR-706 east through Ashford to the Nisqually Entrance of the park, then continue about 6.5 miles to Longmire. The center is in the Longmire Administration Building, across from the museum.

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (Methow Valley Ranger District)
storedPass: Not needed at the SR-20 roadside pullout used for the Wine Spires. A Northwest Forest Pass is required at Washington Pass Overlook, Blue Lake, and Cutthroat trailheads — $5/day or $30/annual (America the Beautiful pass also honored).
drive: East of Washington Pass on SR-20, pullout on right/south side of highway

names: PCT North Trailhead, Snoqualmie Pass (I-90 Exit 52)
landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Snoqualmie Ranger District)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass ($30/yr) or America the Beautiful pass, or a $5/day pass at developed trailheads.

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, Methow Valley Ranger District (within the Lake Chelan-Sawtooth Wilderness)
drive: From the Reynolds Creek Trailhead (~3,100-3,170 ft, reached via Forest Road 4435, which crosses the Twisp River near Mystery Campground before the Spur 4435-015 turnoff to the trailhead), the route follows Reynolds Creek Trail #402, an unmaintained, primitive Forest Service trail entering the Lake Chelan-Sawtooth Wilderness.

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, Wenatchee River Ranger District (Leavenworth, WA)
drive: Begin at the Old Merritt Lake Trailhead off US-2 (~2,950 ft).

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, Wenatchee River Ranger District
storedPass: None at the primary US-2 trailhead; Northwest Forest Pass required at some alternate trailheads (e.g., Kahler Glen/Nason Ridge Trailhead).
drive: From the Rock Mountain Trail #1587 pullout on US-2 (small dirt lot on the north side of the highway near the powerlines, no facilities), the trail launches immediately uphill on what was formerly a service road.

landManager: Gifford Pinchot National Forest (USFS)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass
drive: From Randle, drive south on Forest Road 25 to Forest Road 2551, just south of Elk Pass, then east on FR2551 for about 1.6 miles to an unmarked spur on the left; park at or just past the spur.

landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Mount Baker Ranger District) — Mount Baker Wilderness
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at most trailheads — $30/year or $5/day.
drive: From Sedro-Woolley, drive WA-9 north to Acme, turn right (east) onto Mosquito Lake Road and follow it about 9 miles, cross the Middle Fork Nooksack River and continue onto Forest Road 38 for about 11 miles to the Elbow Lake trailhead. Since July 2026 Forest Road 38 has been closed to vehicles by a washout at milepost 7.
From Interstate 90 exit 52, turn onto State Route 906, then continue onto Erste Strasse (Alpental Access Road) and follow it for 1.1 miles to a left turn into the Alpental lots.

names: Dailey Prairie logging-road gate (Middle Fork Nooksack)
landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Mt. Baker Ranger District) — Mount Baker Wilderness
storedPass: No developed fee trailhead here — FR 38 gate/pullout is an undeveloped roadside parking spot; no Northwest Forest Pass required.
drive: From the Middle Fork Nooksack bridge gate: bike the Dailey Prairie logging roads to the north-side climbers' paths (gate status changes year to year — verify before the trip)

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, Wenatchee River Ranger District
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful pass required at developed trailheads.
drive: Park at the Yodelin lot on US 2 (the former Yodelin ski area's lot, now used for overflow parking, roughly 1.7 miles from the Stevens Pass Ski Area pedestrian overpass, around milepost 60).

names: FR-63 roadside pullout east of Galena
landManager: Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest, Skykomish Ranger District (Wild Sky Wilderness)
storedPass: No pass needed at the FR-63 roadside pullout east of Galena.
drive: Drive US-2 to Skykomish, then north on Beckler River Road (FR-65) for about 15 miles; turn left (west) onto FR-63 and follow it about 4.6 miles to where it crosses the North Fork Skykomish River again; park at the unmarked pullout on the rise just past the bridge, about a mile east of Galena. Since the December 2025 floods Beckler River Road has been closed beyond Jack Pass and the North Fork Skykomish bridge on FR-63 is out, so this pullout cannot be reached by car right now.

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, Methow Valley Ranger District (Buttermilk Creek/Twisp approach); the Prince Creek/Chelan Summit Trail approach falls under the Chelan Ranger District on the Lake Chelan side.
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass (or America the Beautiful/Interagency Pass) required to park at the West Fork Buttermilk Creek Trailhead.
drive: Trailhead is the West Fork Buttermilk Creek Trailhead (Trail #411), reached via Twisp River Road ~10.7-10.8 miles from Twisp, then left on Buttermilk Creek Road, staying left onto East Buttermilk Road (Forest Road 43) for roughly 4 miles, then right onto the Road 500 spur for about 2.7 miles to the road-end trailhead at about 3,960 ft.
From Interstate 90 exit 52, turn onto State Route 906, then continue onto Erste Strasse (Alpental Access Road) and follow it for 1.1 miles to a left turn into the lot just below the main lodges.

landManager: North Cascades National Park (National Park Service)
storedPass: No federal recreation pass required for the park; backcountry permit required for overnight camping.

landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest, Alpine Lakes Wilderness (Middle Fork Snoqualmie side)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass / Interagency pass
drive: From the drivable end of the Middle Fork Snoqualmie Road (NF-56)

landManager: National Park Service — Olympic National Park (Olympic Wilderness)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful interagency pass to park at the Upper Dungeness Trailhead, which is on Olympic National Forest land.
drive: Drive Hwy 101 to just before Sequim Bay State Park, turn onto Louella Rd, then Palo Alto Rd (becomes FR 28) for about 6 miles, turn right on FR 2880 along the Dungeness River, then in 1.7 miles turn left on FR 2870 and continue roughly 6.5-9 miles (gravel, winds steeply down to a river crossing) to the large Dungeness/Royal Basin trailhead lot (picnic table, vault toilet).

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, Methow Valley Ranger District — within the Lake Chelan-Sawtooth Wilderness
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass
drive: From the Foggy Dew Trailhead (3,400 ft)

landManager: Olympic National Park (National Park Service)
storedPass: NPS wilderness camping permit (Recreation.gov) required for overnight stays; a day climb does not need a wilderness permit but a park entrance fee/pass applies.

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (Methow Valley Ranger District)
drive: Head northwest from the Mazama store on Lost River Road for 1.5 miles and pull into the big lot on the right-hand side. The lot is on private land that climbers may use by permission, so do not camp there.

landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Skykomish Ranger District)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful pass required at developed trailheads.
drive: From Skykomish, drive US-2 east about 12 miles; just as the highway crests a deep curve over Tunnel Creek, turn right onto FR-6095 (possible only from the eastbound lane) and go about 1.3 miles to the trailhead.

landManager: Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Skykomish Ranger District) — Alpine Lakes Wilderness
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass
drive: From Skykomish, drive US-2 east about 10 miles to an unsigned right turn near milepost 58.7, just past the old railroad community of Scenic; cross the railroad tracks, turn right, and follow the narrow dirt road about 0.3 mile to the trailhead.

landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Mt. Baker Ranger District) — Mount Baker Wilderness, with some upper routes crossing into North Cascades National Park
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at most trailheads — $30/year or $5/day.
drive: From Glacier, drive east on Mount Baker Highway (SR 542) for about 12 miles and turn left onto Twin Lakes Road (FR 3065) at the end of the maintenance facility. Follow it about 4.5 miles to the trailhead parking.

names: Unsigned climbers' path off FS Road 56
landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Snoqualmie Ranger District)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass ($30/yr) or America the Beautiful pass, or a $5/day pass at developed trailheads.

drive: From South Canyon Road in Ellensburg, drive Umtanum Road about 10 miles southwest to the trailhead.
From Enumclaw drive SR 410 east toward Crystal Mountain to the signed Skookum Falls viewpoint pullout on the right, about 9.5 miles south of Greenwater.

landManager: North Cascades National Park (NPS); trailhead access via Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass or Interagency pass required at the Hannegan Trailhead
drive: From Bellingham, drive SR-542 east about 46 miles, which is 13 miles past Glacier, and just before the third crossing of the Nooksack River turn left onto FR-32, then follow it 5.3 miles to its end at Hannegan Campground, where the trailhead is.
From White Pass drive east on US 12 for about 2.2 miles to Dog Lake and park near it; the Clear Creek Falls overlook lot is likely snowed in during winter.
